script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for October 23. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Before science, we asked authorities.  Now we ask nature directly—through observation and experiment.  The universe doesn't lie, doesn't have opinions, doesn't play favorites.

Good science starts with good questions—specific enough to test, open enough to surprise. 'How does this work?' 'What would happen if?' The question frames the investigation. Experiments control variables to isolate causes.  Change one thing, keep others constant, observe what happens.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: The universe doesn't lie.  Ask the right questions and observe carefully, and reality will teach you.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Personal Experiment - What Can Reality Teach You?.

Here's your activity: Pick a question about your life you don't know the answer to. Formulate it clearly. What test or observation would give you an answer? Design a small experiment and let reality teach you. This helps you apply scientific inquiry to personal questions.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about asking nature questions can be applied to personal experiment - what can reality teach you?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
